messages:
Anya: Quick heads-up: my Go sample app leaks a goroutine when I cancel a generator stream with a context timeout.
Anya: Flow: ctx, client.GenerateStream(ctx, req), loop Recv(); when ctx expires Recv() blocks forever.
Micah: Which go-sdk version? We did a stream refactor recently.
Anya: v0.9.3 (go.mod).
Sam: We moved to a background reader + token channel. If the reader is blocked on Read, ctx cancel won't wake it unless transport is closed.
Devon: Sounds like transport.Close() on ctx cancel is the minimal fix so socket.Read unblocks.
Anya: I hacked a workaround: goroutine that waits on ctx.Done() and calls stream.Close(), but we shouldn’t make callers do that.
Julie: Also saw inconsistent Recv() semantics: sometimes io.EOF, sometimes context.Canceled, sometimes a net error. Docs need to standardize.
Micah: Immediate plan: add transport.Close() on ctx cancel. Long-term: redesign generator ergonomics to iterator-style API.
Micah: Proposal sketch:
```
// iterator-style stream
type GeneratorStream interface {
  Next(ctx context.Context) bool
  Token() Token
  Err() error // io.EOF for normal end, context.Canceled if cancelled
  Close() error
}
```
Sam: That makes loops read-friendly and makes cancel handling explicit.
Devon: Also add a quickstart snippet demonstrating context timeouts + stream.Close() until API changes land.
Anya: I’ll add a tiny sample under dev-examples that spins up a slow fake server, uses a short timeout, and asserts no goroutine leak (runtime.NumGoroutine check).
Micah: I’ll file an issue with the proposed API and push a small PR to call transport.Close() on ctx cancel as an interim fix.
